world.title: MALAWI: Malawi: Prelate Ordains Thirteen Deacons, Urges them to Embrace Sacrifice and Service
world.description:
By Brenard Mwanza
Bishop Yohane Suzgo Nyirenda of the Catholic Diocese of Mzuzu has called on newly ordained deacons to embrace a life of sacrificial love, deep humility, and faithful commitment in their ministry, urging them to model their service on Christ the Servant who gave Himself for the salvation of humanity.
Speaking on Saturday, May 23 May, during the Eucharistic Celebration for the ordination of thirteen seminarians to the diaconate at St. Peter’s Major Seminary in the Diocese of Zomba, Bishop Nyirenda reminded the candidates that the diaconate is not a call to honour or privilege, but a vocation of selfless service in imitation of Jesus Christ, who came to save humanity.
He encouraged the deacons to remain steadfast in prayer, obedience, and dedication to the Gospel, offering their lives fully to God for the salvation of souls.
The bishop further appealed to the faithful to continue supporting seminaries and houses of formation, noting that the formation of priests, sisters, and religious brothers remains a shared responsibility of the entire Church.
On efforts toward self-reliance, Bishop Nyirenda said the Church is working to ensure that its institutions are sustained through the generosity and contributions of the faithful, adding that while progress is being made, greater commitment is still required.
“All Christians are encouraged to support St. Peter’s Major Seminary, Kachebere Major Seminary, and the minor seminaries. Let us respond positively to the appeal of rectors and formators by opening our hearts and hands generously for the formation of priests, seminarians, sisters, and brothers,” he said.
The candidates came from the Archdioceses of Blantyre and Lilongwe, the Dioceses of Chikwawa, Mzuzu, Zomba, Mangochi and Dedza, with two of them belonging to the Capuchin Congregation.
